title: Understand Ratios
contentObjective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.
languageObjective: I can explain a comparison using the words ratio, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and colon notation.

I notice the whole batch is made of ___.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Chef Reyes's Cookie Recipe
revealWordProblem.text: Chef Reyes's signature cookie recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. The students are preparing one batch of dough. Question: What is the ratio of flour to sugar in the recipe, and what is the part-to-whole ratio of flour to the total cups of these two ingredients?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The ratio of flour to sugar is 3:2 (part-to-part). The total cups of these two ingredients is 3 + 2 = 5, so the part-to-whole ratio of flour to total is 3:5.

turnAndTalk.question: Chef Reyes's signature cookie recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. How would you describe how these two ingredient amounts compare?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar.

stems.en: For every ___ cups of flour there are ___ cups of sugar.
stems.es: Por cada ___ tazas de harina hay ___ tazas de azúcar.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer names that flour and sugar are being compared and states the relationship as 3 to 2 (or 'for every 3 flour, 2 sugar'), not just that there is more flour.
turnAndTalk.extend: Would the ratio still describe the same recipe if you wrote it as sugar to flour instead of flour to sugar? Justify why the order changes the ratio but not the recipe.
extendStems: The order matters because ___, so flour to sugar (___) is different from sugar to flour (___).
Both describe the same recipe because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: At the Prep Station you sorted the chef's statements. What made something a ratio instead of NOT a ratio (like '12 cookies on the tray')?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A ratio compares two quantities, but '12 cookies' is only one amount.

stems.en: This is a ratio because it compares ___ to ___.
stems.es: Esto es una razón porque compara ___ con ___.

stems.en: This is NOT a ratio because it only ___.
stems.es: Esto NO es una razón porque solo ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for the idea that a ratio must compare two quantities (using 'to', 'for every', 'out of', or a colon), while a single count or a description is not a comparison.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique this claim: 'The oven is set to 350°F is a ratio because it has the word to in it.' Is the student right? Defend your answer.
extendStems: The student is wrong because the word 'to' alone does not ___; a ratio must ___.
350°F is just ___, not a comparison of ___ and ___.

turnAndTalk.question: In Menu Planning the cafeteria wants 3 main dishes for every 2 side dishes. How is this the same kind of thinking as Chef Reyes's flour-to-sugar ratio?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Both use a ratio to keep two amounts in the same comparison.

stems.en: This is like our ratio work because ___ and ___ are compared.
stems.es: Esto es como nuestro trabajo con razones porque se comparan ___ y ___.

stems.en: The ratio of main dishes to side dishes is ___.
stems.es: La razón de platos principales a guarniciones es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer identifies the 3:2 part-to-part ratio and explains that the cafeteria keeps that comparison the same even when amounts grow, just like the recipe.
turnAndTalk.extend: If the cafeteria has 10 side dishes, generalize how you could figure out the main dishes — and explain why simply 'adding 1 more main than side' would NOT work.
extendStems: I can scale the ratio 3:2 by ___, so 10 sides means ___ mains.
Adding 1 each time does not work because a ratio must ___, not ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Understand Ratios, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A ratio compares two quantities, and the order you write them in matters.

stems.en: This is a ratio because it compares ___ to ___.
stems.es: Esto es una razón porque compara ___ con ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.1 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

mission.title: The Signature Recipe
mission.story: You just earned your apron at Chef Academy. Head Chef Reyes is trusting you with her signature cookie recipe — 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. Before service begins, you must read every recipe like a pro by mastering ratios, or the whole kitchen falls behind.
mission.objective: Compare ingredient amounts using ratios so every batch comes out exactly right.

scenes.name: Recipe Card
scenes.text: Read Chef Reyes's recipe and notice how flour and sugar compare.

scenes.name: Kitchen Glossary
scenes.text: Learn the language of ratios: comparison, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and colon notation.

scenes.name: Prep Station
scenes.text: Sort the chef's statements — which are real ratios and which are not?

scenes.name: Cookie Line
scenes.text: Fill the cookie orders. The kitchen adapts the difficulty to keep you cooking.

scenes.name: Menu Planning
scenes.text: Use ratios to scale a real cafeteria menu of mains and sides.

scenes.name: Service Review
scenes.text: Plate your final dish and show Chef Reyes what you learned.

finale.title: Service Approved!
finale.text: Every batch came out balanced and the dining room is full. Chef Reyes just named you sous-chef of Chef Academy — all because you can read a recipe in ratios.

launch.narrative: Welcome to Chef Academy! Head Chef Reyes is teaching new students how to read recipes like a pro. Her signature cookie recipe calls for 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. Before the students can start baking, they need to understand how these ingredient amounts compare to each other.
noticePrompts: What two ingredients are being compared in the recipe?
How could you describe the relationship between flour and sugar?
Is the amount of flour more than, less than, or equal to the amount of sugar?
wonderPrompts: What if we compared the sugar to the flour instead — would the ratio change?
Could we compare one ingredient to the total amount of both?
launch.contextImage: A kitchen counter with measuring cups showing 3 cups of flour and 2 cups of sugar beside a recipe card

conceptIntro.heading: What is a ratio?
conceptIntro.intro: A ratio compares two amounts. It tells how much of one thing there is for another thing.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A ratio compares two quantities, and the order you write them in matters.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Chef Reyes uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar.
I am comparing two amounts: flour and sugar.
I write flour to sugar, in that order, as 3 to 2.
In colon notation I write it as 3:2.
So the ratio of flour to sugar is 3:2.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A bowl has 4 apples and 1 orange. What two amounts are we comparing?
We write apples to oranges in order: 4 to 1.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will sort the chef's statements into ratios and not-ratios.
Remember: a real ratio compares two amounts.

explore.instructions: Chef Reyes wrote several comparisons on the board. Sort them into two groups: statements that ARE ratios and statements that are NOT ratios.

items.text: 4 eggs for every 1 stick of butter
5 red apples out of 8 total apples
There are 12 cookies on the tray

discourse.prompt: What makes something a ratio? How did you decide which statements to sort into each group?
discourse.sentenceFrame: A ratio compares ___ to ___ using words like ___ or symbols like ___.

approaching.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
approaching.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
approaching.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta: pide leche a crema, exactamente en ese orden.
En una razón, la cantidad que se nombra primero va primero. Halla la cantidad de leche y la de crema antes de escribir nada.
Subraya las dos cantidades: leche = 4 tazas, crema = 1 taza. Escríbelas en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.

approaching.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
approaching.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: Notice the word 'total' — this is a part-to-WHOLE ratio, not banana-to-strawberry.
First find the total fruit by adding strawberries and bananas. Then compare bananas to that total.
Add 6 + 2 to get the total fruit. Then write the bananas' number first, followed by that total.
approaching.stemEs: El chef Reyes usa 6 fresas y 2 plátanos en un licuado. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de plátanos con respecto a la fruta total?
hintsEs: Fíjate en la palabra 'total': esta es una razón parte a TODO, no de plátano a fresa.
Primero halla la fruta total sumando las fresas y los plátanos. Luego compara los plátanos con ese total.
Suma 6 + 2 para obtener la fruta total. Luego escribe primero el número de plátanos, seguido de ese total.

approaching.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
approaching.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
hints: The problem tells you girls (18) and the whole class (30) — but it asks about BOYS to girls.
Find the number of boys first by subtracting the girls from the class total. Then write boys first, girls second.
Subtract 30 − 18 to find the boys. Put that number first in the ratio, then 18 for the girls.
approaching.stemEs: En un salón de 30 estudiantes, 18 son niñas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de niños a niñas?
hintsEs: El problema te da las niñas (18) y toda la clase (30), pero pregunta por los NIÑOS a las niñas.
Halla primero el número de niños restando las niñas del total de la clase. Luego escribe niños primero y niñas después.
Resta 30 − 18 para hallar los niños. Pon ese número primero en la razón y luego 18 para las niñas.

approaching.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
approaching.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
hints: Re-read: the question asks for dogs to cats, in that order.
A ratio only uses the two amounts being compared — don't add them together. Match the order to the words.
Dogs are named first, so their count (5) starts the ratio. Then write the cats' count after the colon.
approaching.stemEs: Una tienda de mascotas tiene 5 perros y 9 gatos. ¿Cuál es la razón de perros a gatos?
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: la pregunta pide perros a gatos, en ese orden.
Una razón solo usa las dos cantidades que se comparan; no las sumes. Haz que el orden coincida con las palabras.
Los perros se nombran primero, así que su cantidad (5) empieza la razón. Luego escribe la cantidad de gatos después de los dos puntos.

approaching.instructions: Sort each statement: does it describe a ratio or NOT describe a ratio?

items.text: There are 15 chairs in the room

approaching.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: A ratio must COMPARE two amounts. Ask each card: does it mention two quantities, or just one?
Look for compare words like 'for every' or 'to.' A single count ('15 chairs') or an opinion ('delicious') compares nothing.
Test the first card: does '7 pencils for every 3 erasers' name TWO amounts being compared? That answer tells you its pile.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada afirmación: ¿describe una razón o NO describe una razón?
hintsEs: Una razón debe COMPARAR dos cantidades. Pregúntale a cada tarjeta: ¿menciona dos cantidades o solo una?
Busca palabras de comparación como 'por cada' o 'a'. Un solo conteo ('15 sillas') o una opinión ('delicioso') no compara nada.
Prueba la primera tarjeta: ¿'7 lápices por cada 3 borradores' nombra DOS cantidades que se comparan? Esa respuesta te dice su montón.

approaching.title: Spot Marco's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A recipe uses 2 cups of oil and 5 cups of water. Write the ratio of oil to water.

approaching.correctWork: Order matters: 'oil to water' lists oil first. The correct ratio is 2:5, not 5:2.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which amount should come first in 'oil to water'?
Oil is named first, so write the oil amount (2) first: 2:5.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each statement — is it a part-to-part ratio or a part-to-whole ratio?

items.text: 3 boys to 5 girls in cooking class
4 vegetarian dishes out of 10 total dishes
3 sweet items out of 10 total items

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: Look for the words 'out of' or 'total' — those signal a comparison to the WHOLE group.
Ask each card: are BOTH numbers pieces of the group (part-to-part), or is the second number the whole group (part-to-whole)?
Try '3 boys to 5 girls': boys and girls are each just one part of the class — no total is named. Which pile does that point to?
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada afirmación: ¿es una razón parte a parte o una razón parte a todo?
hintsEs: Busca las palabras 'de un total de' o 'total': esas señalan una comparación con TODO el grupo.
Pregúntale a cada tarjeta: ¿son AMBOS números partes del grupo (parte a parte), o el segundo número es el grupo entero (parte a todo)?
Prueba '3 niños a 5 niñas': niños y niñas son cada uno solo una parte de la clase; no se nombra un total. ¿A qué montón apunta eso?

onLevel.stem: A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
onLevel.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
That compares pineapple to the total (5 + 3 + 2). The question compares pineapple to melon only.
hints: Three fruits are listed, but the question only compares pineapple and melon — the grapes are extra info.
Pick out just the two amounts you need, then write them in the order the question names: pineapple first.
Circle the pineapple count (3) and the melon count (5). Write them in the order 'pineapple to melon.'
onLevel.stemEs: Una ensalada de frutas tiene 5 trozos de melón, 3 trozos de piña y 2 uvas. ¿Cuál es la razón de piña a melón?
hintsEs: Se enumeran tres frutas, pero la pregunta solo compara la piña y el melón: las uvas son información extra.
Escoge solo las dos cantidades que necesitas y escríbelas en el orden que nombra la pregunta: la piña primero.
Encierra la cantidad de piña (3) y la de melón (5). Escríbelas en el orden 'piña a melón'.

onLevel.instructions: Complete the table by writing each ratio in all three forms.
hints: Look at the finished row: '4 cats to 7 dogs' becomes 4 to 7, then 4:7, then 4/7 — same numbers, three costumes.
Keep the numbers and their order the same in every column; only the symbols change (the word 'to', a colon, a fraction bar).
Start with row 2: which number comes first, the 9 red or the 15 total? Keep that order and just change the symbol in each column.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Completa la tabla escribiendo cada razón en las tres formas.
hintsEs: Mira la fila terminada: '4 gatos a 7 perros' se vuelve 4 a 7, luego 4:7, luego 4/7 — los mismos números con tres disfraces.
Conserva los números y su orden en cada columna; solo cambian los símbolos (la palabra 'a', dos puntos, una barra de fracción).
Empieza con la fila 2: ¿qué número va primero, los 9 rojos o el total de 15? Conserva ese orden y solo cambia el símbolo en cada columna.

onLevel.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
onLevel.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: The word 'total' means this is part-to-whole — compare trucks to ALL vehicles, not to cars.
First find the total number of vehicles by adding cars and trucks. The trucks' number goes first.
Add 10 + 6 to find the total vehicles. Then write 6 (the trucks) first and that total second.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estacionamiento tiene 10 carros y 6 camionetas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de camionetas con respecto al total de vehículos?
hintsEs: La palabra 'total' significa que esto es parte a todo: compara los camiones con TODOS los vehículos, no con los carros.
Primero halla el número total de vehículos sumando carros y camiones. El número de camiones va primero.
Suma 10 + 6 para hallar el total de vehículos. Luego escribe 6 (los camiones) primero y ese total después.

onLevel.title: Spot Dana's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A bowl has 3 apples and 4 oranges. Write the part-to-whole ratio of apples to total fruit.

onLevel.correctWork: A part-to-whole ratio compares the part to the total, not to the other part. The correct ratio is 3:7 (3 apples out of 7 total), not 3:4.
hints: Look at Step 3. Should the second number be the oranges (4) or the total (7)?
Part-to-whole uses the total, so apples to total fruit is 3:7.

extending.title: Find Aliya's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A trail mix has 6 almonds, 4 raisins, and 2 cashews. Write the ratio of raisins to total pieces.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The ratio of raisins to total is 4:8.

extending.correctWork: The total is 12, not 8. The correct ratio is 4:12.
hints: Look at Step 3. Does 8 match the total Aliya found in Step 2?
The total is 12 pieces, so the part-to-whole ratio should use 12, not 8.

extending.stem: A bag of marbles has 8 red, 6 blue, and 4 green marbles. Write three different ratios using these quantities: one part-to-part ratio, one part-to-whole ratio, and explain the difference.
extending.sampleAnswer: Part-to-part: red to blue = 8:6. Part-to-whole: green to total = 4:18. The difference is that part-to-part compares two individual groups, while part-to-whole compares one group to the entire collection (8 + 6 + 4 = 18).
extending.hint: Remember to explain which type each ratio is.
hints: You need THREE things: a part-to-part ratio, a part-to-whole ratio, and an explanation of how they differ.
Part-to-part compares two colors. Part-to-whole compares one color to ALL marbles — so you'll need the total first.
Start by finding the whole: add 8 + 6 + 4. Then pick any two colors for your part-to-part ratio, like red to blue.
extending.stemEs: Una bolsa de canicas tiene 8 rojas, 6 azules y 4 verdes. Escribe tres razones diferentes con estas cantidades: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo, y explica la diferencia.
hintsEs: Necesitas TRES cosas: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo y una explicación de en qué se diferencian.
Parte a parte compara dos colores. Parte a todo compara un color con TODAS las canicas, así que necesitarás el total primero.
Empieza hallando el todo: suma 8 + 6 + 4. Luego escoge dos colores cualesquiera para tu razón parte a parte, como rojo a azul.

extending.instructions: A classroom has 12 boys and 8 girls. Sort each ratio statement as either CORRECT or INCORRECT.
extending.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: First figure out the class total from 12 boys and 8 girls — some cards secretly use it.
For each card, check two things: are the numbers right, AND does the order match the words (boys first if it says 'boys to')?
Test 'Boys to girls = 12:8': boys are 12, girls are 8, and boys are named first. Does the card's ratio match that order?

optionalActivity.name: Culinary Ratio Challenge Room

optional.stem: Station 1 — Sauce Bench: Chef Reyes mixes 3 cups of tomato sauce with 2 cups of cream. What is the ratio of tomato sauce to cream?
optional.explanation: A ratio compares the two amounts in the order named. Tomato sauce to cream = 3 to 2, written 3:2.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
optional.stemEs: Estación 1 — Mesa de salsas: El chef Reyes mezcla 3 tazas de salsa de tomate con 2 tazas de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de salsa de tomate a crema?

optional.stem: Station 2 — Fruit Tray: A tray holds 4 strawberries and 6 blueberries. What is the part-to-whole ratio of strawberries to total berries?
optional.explanation: Total berries = 4 + 6 = 10. The part-to-whole ratio of strawberries to total is 4:10.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
optional.stemEs: Estación 2 — Bandeja de fruta: Una bandeja tiene 4 fresas y 6 arándanos. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de fresas con respecto al total de bayas?

optional.instructions: Station 3 — Recipe Board: Sort each kitchen comparison as a part-to-part ratio or a part-to-whole ratio.

items.text: 3 cups flour out of 5 cups total
4 sweet dishes out of 9 total dishes

optional.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
optional.instructionsEs: Estación 3 — Tablero de recetas: Clasifica cada comparación de la cocina como razón parte a parte o parte a todo.

optional.label: Station 4 — Plating Match: Match each kitchen picture or context to the ratio that describes it in colon form.
optional.labelEs: Estación 4 — Emplatado: Une cada imagen o contexto de la cocina con la razón que lo describe en forma de dos puntos.

optional.stem: Station 5 — Soup Pot: A soup uses 8 cups of broth and 3 cups of noodles. What is the ratio of broth to noodles?
optional.explanation: Broth is named first, then noodles, so the ratio is 8 to 3, written 8:3.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Fix the Mislabeled Recipe Ratio

workedExample.label: Read the recipe
workedExample.work: Chef Reyes's salad uses 5 cups of lettuce and 3 cups of spinach. Write the part-to-part ratio of lettuce to spinach.

workedExample.label: Label the ratio
workedExample.work: This is a part-to-part ratio of lettuce to spinach.

optional.correctWork: Part-to-part compares lettuce to spinach, not lettuce to the total. The correct ratio is 5:3 (the 8 would only be used for a part-to-whole ratio like 5:8).
hints: Look at Step 3. A part-to-part ratio compares one part to another part — should the second number be the spinach amount or the total?
Lettuce to spinach uses 5 and 3, so the part-to-part ratio is 5:3. Use 8 only when comparing a part to the whole.
Now create your own recipe ratio: 'My recipe uses ___ cups of ___ to ___ cups of ___, so the part-to-part ratio is ___:___.'

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Understand Ratios is writing the ratio in the wrong order: Chef Reyes's cookie recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar, but when asked for the ratio of flour to sugar, some students write 2:3 instead of 3:2 because they default to whichever ingredient comes to mind first instead of the order named in the question. The ratio 3:2 means 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar; 2:3 would mean only 2 cups of flour for every 3 cups of sugar — a much soupier dough. Always match the order of your ratio to the order the question names: "flour to sugar" means the flour number comes first, giving 3:2.

diagram.title: Cafeteria Menu Ratio 3:2
diagram.caption: Each box is one dish; the mains row has 3 boxes for every 2 in the sides row, showing the 3:2 ratio the cafeteria keeps.

connect.scenario: The school cafeteria is planning a new lunch menu. They want to offer 3 main dishes for every 2 side dishes. If they have 10 side dishes, the cafeteria manager needs to figure out how many main dishes to prepare.
connect.prompt: This is like our ratio work because ___ and ___ are related by ___.

check.stem: Keeping the 3:2 ratio, how many main dishes go with 10 side dishes?
check.explanation: 10 sides ÷ 2 = a scale factor of 5. Multiply the mains by that same 5: 3 × 5 = 15 main dishes.

check.stem: What kind of ratio is 3 mains to 2 sides?
choices: Part-to-part, because it compares two separate groups
Part-to-whole, because it compares mains to all dishes
A rate, because it uses different units
check.explanation: Mains and sides are two separate parts, so 3:2 is part-to-part. Part-to-whole would be 3 mains to 5 total dishes.

check.stem: With 15 mains and 10 sides, what is the ratio of mains to TOTAL dishes?
check.explanation: 15 + 10 = 25 total dishes, and 15:25 simplifies to 3:5. That is a part-to-whole ratio.

connect.modelAnswer: The ratio 3 mains : 2 sides stays the same no matter how much food the cafeteria makes. With 10 side dishes the scale factor is 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so they need 3 × 5 = 15 main dishes. That gives 15:10, which simplifies right back to 3:2.

exitTicket.stem: A bag of trail mix contains 8 peanuts and 5 raisins. What is the ratio of raisins to total pieces?
exitTicket.explanation: Total pieces = 8 + 5 = 13. The ratio of raisins to total is 5:13.
choiceFeedback: That's peanuts to raisins — the question asks raisins to TOTAL.
That compares raisins to peanuts, not raisins to the whole bag.
You reversed it — put raisins first, then the total.
hints: Careful — this asks for raisins compared to ALL the pieces in the bag, not to the peanuts.
Find the total first by adding peanuts and raisins, then write the raisins' number before the total.
Add 8 + 5 to get the total pieces. Start the ratio with 5 (the raisins), then put that total after the colon.

questions.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
questions.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.

questions.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
questions.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.

questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
questions.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
